title: Merge Coincident Nodes
statement: Geometry imported from several drawings has nodes that should be one node but sit a hair apart. Two nodes are coincident when the distance between them is at most the tolerance, and coincidence spreads: if A merges with B and B merges with C then A, B and C all become one node, even if A and C are further apart than the tolerance. Return how many distinct nodes remain after merging.
constraints: distance is straight-line, and exactly equal to the tolerance still merges
hints: The obvious approach is to snap every coordinate onto a grid of tolerance-sized cells and count the distinct cells. Try that on three points spaced 0.6 apart with a tolerance of 0.7 and see what it does.
Merging is transitive, which is what breaks snapping: a chain of nodes each within tolerance of the next is a single node however long the chain gets.

That is exactly a connected-components question. Union every pair within tolerance and count the surviving roots. Compare squared distances against the squared tolerance and you never need a square root.
